Consumer sentiment fell 8% in August compared to last month, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. Released Friday, the latest sentiment reading ended two consecutive months of improvement as Americans feel the effects of the Iran war pushing up fuel, energy and food prices. [...] “Consumers are feeling worse about the economy this month and pessimistic about future inflation. There’s little doubt this movement is due, in part, to the Iran war roller coaster,” NerdWallet Senior Economist Elizabeth Renter said in a statement following the University of Michigan survey
results.title: Consumer sentiment and retail spending are down

results.content:
The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers reported that its final Index of Consumer Sentiment fell to 51.7 in August, down 6.3% from July's reading of 55.2 and 11.2% below its level a year earlier. The decline snapped two consecutive months of improvement following a record low in May, amid what survey director Joanne Hsu described as "continued worries that inflation will remain elevated for the foreseeable future."
